drawings.description: feuille de croquis au crayon. En haut à droite « McL » et « $\times M'U$ », une lettre « A ». À gauche, un morphisme $X \to k$ et $k \to Y$ en équerre, puis $X' \to X$ avec une flèche oblique $X' \to k$ marquée \uncertain{« $\phi$ »}. En bas, deux esquisses $Y \to X$ au-dessus de $k$ et $Y' \to X'$ au-dessus de $k'$, une flèche $k \to k'$ barrée d'un petit cercle hachuré ; à droite un carré $X \leftarrow X$, $K$, $k'$, $k \leftarrow K$, un $X$ entouré.
drawings.kind: sheet of pencil sketches of arrow diagrams
drawings.notes: Redrawn with the sheet turned 180 degrees, the way the transcription reads it: then every letter is upright (McL, x M'U, A, X, k, Y, K, phi). Upper left: X over a vertical stroke down to k, and a horizontal stroke from k to Y (no arrowheads on the page). Below: X' -> X, an oblique arrow from X' down to k marked phi (the phi at the far left edge), and a vertical stroke from X down to that k. Upper right: McL, x M'U, and A with a faint short arrow after it. Lower half: Y -> X with a diagonal and a vertical stroke down to k; Y' -> X' with a curve and a vertical stroke down to k'; the stroke k -> k' crossed by a small hatched circle inside a faint larger ring, and a vertical arrow coming down across it; two long faint horizontal strokes under them at the left. Lower right: the square k', X (ringed) <- X, K, the arrow from the ringed X down to k, k -- K (no arrowhead on the page), the heavy vertical from K, the stroke from k' downwards, a faint arc over the top and a faint loop. Left out on purpose: the square Y <-h- Y', f, f', X <-g- X' in the middle right with its ring, "V'", "g(U')" and "U' != emptyset", which the transcription typesets as text (tikzcd and note) after the drawing mark; a faint dot with a short stroke left of A; the page number. Still differs: the faint pencil loops at the lower right are approximate. Redrawn 2026-11-09 (issue 128): to check again.
drawings.disagreement: None on the orientation: turned 180 degrees, the sheet reads as the transcription says (the earlier redraw drew it the other way up). Two details the description does not name: a vertical arrow coming down across the stroke k -> k' next to the hatched circle, and a faint short arrow after the A.
drawings.orientation: rotated 180: the sheet is redrawn turned, as the transcription reads it

drawings.description: un cercle traversé d'un diamètre horizontal, un point au centre.
drawings.notes: A circle (stroke doubled at the upper left), a horizontal diameter, a heavy point at the centre.

drawings.description: au bas de la page, un réseau de lignes obliques entrecroisées (une rangée de losanges) sur lequel il a écrit en travers : « Dire », « $X$, $Y$ \uncertain{lisses} », « $F_\bullet$, $G_\bullet$ », « \uncertain{revient} \uncertain{à} \uncertain{dire} … \uncertain{d'habitude} », « $i_!(A_U)$, $j_!(A_V)$ », « $i : U\to X$, $j : V\to X$ », « $U$, $V$ », « \ill{} ». Le dessin et l'écriture paraissent superposés ; l'ordre de lecture n'est pas sûr.
drawings.kind: network of crossing oblique lines (row of lozenges) with words written across
drawings.notes: Eleven apexes at their measured places on the page; from each apex a rising line comes up from the bottom and a falling line goes down to the bottom, so that the crossings make the row of lozenges (the first line starts at the left with a blob, the last falling lines stop at the right edge). The lines are drawn straight with two common slopes (rising about 1.9, falling about 1.5, read off the page), so the crossing points are computed rather than traced. Words across, at their places: Dire, X, Y (lisses, uncertain, left out), F, G, i_!(A_U), j_!(A_V), U, V, i : U -> X, j : V -> X. Left out: the phrase written along the top ("revient à dire ... d'habitude", uncertain in the transcription), the illegible word, the small dashes between the lines. Still differs: his lines bend and their slopes vary by a few degrees; the fourth apex (between X, Y and F) is a reading. Redrawn 2026-11-09 (issue 128): to check again.

drawings.description: en marge gauche, le diagramme $T \times_{Z} T' \to T, T' \to X \times_{S} Y = Z$ :

drawings.notes: T x_Z T' at the top, arrows down to T and T', and from these to X x_S Y = Z.
Right triangle, right angle at the top right; the hypotenuse is drawn twice.

drawings.description: deux axes, le long de l'axe horizontal un segment de $0$ à $2d$ marqué de points ; puis un triangle sous une droite de pente $-1$, strié de traits horizontaux, l'abscisse $2d$ marquée.
drawings.kind: axes with a graduated segment; hatched triangle under a line of slope -1
drawings.notes: Above: two axes crossing at a heavy point; along the horizontal one, an open point, a small point (the stretch after it doubled in pencil), and an angle mark at its end over the label 2d; a small open point on the vertical axis just above the origin. Below: axes (the vertical slightly slanted, the origin computed as their meeting point), a thin line of slope about -1, a heavy edge under it from the first step down to the horizontal axis at 2d (heavy point), a staircase of three vertical steps joined by short horizontals, and six horizontal hatching strokes from the vertical axis, each ending on the staircase where it does on the page (the third ends short, at the heavy edge); points on the heavy edge, three small points on the horizontal axis under the steps, a point on the vertical axis. Still differs: the heavy edge is a polyline through the points he marked, his stroke is smoother. Redrawn 2026-11-09 (issue 128): to check again.

drawings.notes: A horizontal segment with a heavy point at its left end and 2d at its right end.

drawings.description: axes $(p, q)$ ; un rectangle de sommets $0$ et $2d$, sa diagonale fortement tracée, la droite $p + q = 0$ prolongée au-delà ; au-dessus, une courte inscription biffée, \uncertain{$q^{4} = q \geq q$}.
drawings.kind: rectangle with heavy diagonal on (p, q) axes
drawings.notes: Vertical axis q and a horizontal line through 0; a rectangle with corners 0 (top left) and 2d (top right and bottom left marked 2d), its diagonal from 0 heavily drawn; a thin line crossing the lower left corner and prolonged beyond the rectangle. Which line is p + q = 0 is the transcription's reading. Omitted as struck: the inscription above (q^4 = q >= q, uncertain). Issue 128, 2026-11-09: struck material left out after a fresh check of the facsimile (struck-out material is not drawn). Redrawn 2026-11-09 (issue 128): to check again.

drawings.description: sous trois des termes de la seconde ligne, des flèches verticales vers $A$ ; sous la première, l'annotation « dualité parfaite triviale (via \uncertain{pureté} …) » ; sous les deux autres, réunies par des arcs, « dualité parfaite ?? ».
drawings.kind: vertical arrows under terms of an exact sequence, with annotations
drawings.notes: Under three terms of the second line (written above; the line is text and not redrawn): two arrows down to A, and under the third a plain vertical stroke down to A (no arrowhead on the page). Left of the first A, a bracket; under it, on four lines, "dualité parfaite triviale (via pureté ...)". The second and third columns are joined by two arcs that come down together towards "dualité parfaite ??" (no arrowheads on the page; the earlier redraw gave them heads). Annotations placed as written. Redrawn 2026-11-09 (issue 128): to check again.

drawings.kind: intervals and an axis with M, 0, N
